```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Swierczek_2023_dexamethasone"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Swierczek_2023_dexamethasone"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13577> (open access, PMC10499420)

The model couples a two-compartment oral PK model of dexamethasone (DEX),
fitted in Monolix to blood concentrations from hospitalized COVID-19
patients, to three indirect-response pools for the inflammatory mediators
TNF-alpha, IL-6 and CRP (paper Figure 1, Eqs 1-6). The PD layer was not fitted
to COVID-19 data: it was assembled from the authors' rat LPS model (Imax,
IC50), human LPS endotoxemia (turnover rate constants and the IL-6 -> CRP
stimulation), and the median biomarker concentrations of COVID-19
non-survivors (baselines), and was then used for population simulation of
four once-daily oral regimens (1.5, 3, 6 and 12 mg for 10 days). The paper's
Supplement 1 reproduces the Monolix model and Simulx simulation code; that code
is the reference used for every structural detail below.

# Population

The PK data are 167 capillary blood DEX concentrations from 27 of the 30
hospitalized COVID-19 patients of Abouir et al. (NCT04996784, Geneva
University Hospitals; mean age 63.5 years, mean body weight 81 kg, men and
women), sampled at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 h after a single fasting 6 mg oral
tablet. Three patients were excluded because their pre-dose concentration
exceeded 50 ng/mL. No individual covariates were available, so the model has
none.

```{r population}
readModelDb("Swierczek_2023_dexamethasone")()$population
```

# Steady-state hold

Without drug, each pool must sit at its kin / kout steady state, which the
paper set to the median biomarker concentrations of COVID-19 non-survivors
(Table 2: 10.9 pg/mL, 59.7 pg/mL, 100.5 mg/L). The kin values are rounded
secondary parameters, so the implied baselines agree with R0 to the rounding
of kin (CRP: kinCRP = 0.0016 is the rounded 0.001603).

```{r steady-state}
mod <- readModelDb("Swierczek_2023_dexamethasone")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ev_hold <- rxode2::et(seq(0, 240, by = 24), cmt = "central")
hold <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_hold))

hold |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 240)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, tnf, il6, crp) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value biomarkers with no dose.")

stopifnot(
  # The pools must not drift without drug (deterministic solve).
  max(abs(hold$tnf / hold$tnf[1] - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(hold$il6 / hold$il6[1] - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(hold$crp / hold$crp[1] - 1)) < 1e-6,
  # Baselines reproduce Table 2 R0 within the rounding of kin.
  abs(hold$tnf[1] / 10.9 - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(hold$il6[1] / 59.7 - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(hold$crp[1] / 100.5 - 1) < 0.005
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated 1000 individuals per regimen in Simulx, sampling every PK
and PD parameter from its distribution. Here 200 individuals per regimen are
simulated (enough to resolve the published success rates to a Monte-Carlo
standard error of about 3.5 percentage points). As in Supplement 1, the first
dose is given at t = 24 h and repeated every 24 h for 10 doses.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230627)

n_per_arm <- 200
regimens <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = factor(c("1.5 mg", "3 mg", "6 mg", "12 mg"),
                   levels = c("1.5 mg", "3 mg", "6 mg", "12 mg")),
  dose = c(1.5, 3, 6, 12)
)
dose_times <- 24 + 24 * (0:9)
obs_times <- seq(0, 264, by = 1)

make_cohort <- function(regimen, dose, n, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = regimen) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(regimens$regimen[i], regimens$dose[i], n_per_arm,
              id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = levels(regimens$regimen)))
```

About 3.5% of simulated subjects draw a negative lag time, because the paper
gives tlag a normal (not log-normal) distribution (mean 0.29 h, SD 0.16 h);
rxode2 then starts their absorption slightly before the nominal dose time.

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4 -- DEX, TNF-alpha, IL-6 and CRP by regimen

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
cutoffs <- tibble::tibble(
  analyte = c("TNF-alpha (pg/mL)", "IL-6 (pg/mL)", "CRP (mg/L)"),
  cutoff = c(7.7, 22.8, 36.7)
)

sim |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, Cc, tnf, il6, crp) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, tnf, il6, crp), names_to = "var") |>
  dplyr::mutate(analyte = dplyr::recode(
    var,
    Cc = "DEX blood (ng/mL)", tnf = "TNF-alpha (pg/mL)",
    il6 = "IL-6 (pg/mL)", crp = "CRP (mg/L)"
  )) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, analyte, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(data = cutoffs, aes(yintercept = cutoff), colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ regimen, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 4 of Swierczek 2023: median and",
                       "5th-95th percentiles; red lines are the treatment",
                       "cut-offs."))
```

## Figure 3 -- CRP under the recommended 6 mg regimen

The paper's Figure 3 overlays published CRP medians and means (Zacharias et
al., Kooistra et al.) on the simulated 6 mg regimen; those observed points are
not tabulated in the article and are not reproduced here.

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "6 mg") |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(crp, 0.05), Q50 = median(crp), Q95 = quantile(crp, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q05), colour = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q95), colour = "blue") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Plasma CRP (mg/L)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 3 of Swierczek 2023: median and",
                       "5th/95th percentiles, 6 mg once daily for 10 days."))
```

## Figure 5 -- treatment end points

The Supplement 1 Simulx `[ENDPOINT]` block scores a subject as a success when
the MAXIMUM biomarker concentration over the 24 h after the assessed dose is
at or below the cut-off (TNF-alpha 7.7 pg/mL, IL-6 22.8 pg/mL, CRP
36.7 mg/L); the cumulative end point requires all three. Day 5 is the 24 h
after the fifth dose (t = 120-144 h), day 10 the 24 h after the tenth
(t = 240-264 h, the Simulx output window).

```{r figure-5}
window_max <- function(sim, from, to, day) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(time >= from, time <= to) |>
    dplyr::group_by(id, regimen) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      TNF = max(tnf) <= 7.7, IL6 = max(il6) <= 22.8, CRP = max(crp) <= 36.7,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cumulative = TNF & IL6 & CRP, day = day)
}
success <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  window_max(sim, 120, 144, "Day 5"),
  window_max(sim, 240, 264, "Day 10")
)

# Figure 5 / Results text: percent of simulated subjects reaching each end point.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~day,     ~endpoint, ~`1.5 mg`, ~`3 mg`, ~`6 mg`, ~`12 mg`,
  "Day 5",  "TNF",     55.0,      65.9,    74.8,    81.2,
  "Day 10", "TNF",     55.0,      65.9,    74.8,    81.2,
  "Day 5",  "IL6",     13.0,      26.5,    38.9,    53.1,
  "Day 10", "IL6",     13.0,      26.5,    38.9,    53.1,
  "Day 5",  "CRP",      5.5,      13.5,    21.6,    34.5,
  "Day 10", "CRP",     20.1,      37.3,    53.5,    67.4
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(day, endpoint), names_to = "regimen",
                      values_to = "published_pct")

rates <- success |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(TNF, IL6, CRP, Cumulative), names_to = "endpoint",
                      values_to = "ok") |>
  dplyr::group_by(day, endpoint, regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated_pct = 100 * mean(ok), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen))

cmp_rates <- rates |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published, by = c("day", "endpoint", "regimen")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = simulated_pct - published_pct)

cmp_rates |>
  dplyr::arrange(endpoint, day, factor(regimen, levels = levels(regimens$regimen))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Day" = day, "End point" = endpoint, "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Simulated (%)" = simulated_pct, "Published (%)" = published_pct,
    "Difference (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
               caption = "Percent of subjects reaching each end point (Figure 5).")

stopifnot(
  # Centre: a wrong IC50, Imax, kout or dose unit shifts every rate by
  # tens of points.
  abs(median(cmp_rates$diff)) < 6,
  # Envelope over 24 rates, each with a Monte-Carlo SE of ~3.5 points at
  # n = 200 per arm; robust to which subjects land in the tails.
  quantile(abs(cmp_rates$diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

```{r figure-5-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
rates |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = levels(regimens$regimen)),
    day = factor(day, levels = c("Day 5", "Day 10")),
    n = simulated_pct / 100 * n_per_arm
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(endpoint, n, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~day) +
  labs(x = "Treatment end point", y = "Subjects reaching end point (of 200)",
       fill = "Regimen",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Swierczek 2023 (200 rather than 1000 per arm).")
```

## Table S1 -- odds ratios against the 6 mg reference (day 10)

```{r table-s1}
odds <- function(p) p / (1 - p)
or_sim <- rates |>
  dplyr::filter(day == "Day 10") |>
  dplyr::group_by(endpoint) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p = pmin(pmax(simulated_pct / 100, 0.001), 0.999),
    OR = odds(p) / odds(p[regimen == "6 mg"])
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen != "6 mg") |>
  dplyr::select(endpoint, regimen, OR)

or_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint,    ~regimen,  ~OR_published,
  "CRP",        "1.5 mg",  0.22,
  "CRP",        "3 mg",    0.52,
  "CRP",        "12 mg",   1.8,
  "IL6",        "1.5 mg",  0.24,
  "IL6",        "3 mg",    0.57,
  "IL6",        "12 mg",   1.78,
  "TNF",        "1.5 mg",  0.41,
  "TNF",        "3 mg",    0.65,
  "TNF",        "12 mg",   1.46,
  "Cumulative", "1.5 mg",  0.23,
  "Cumulative", "3 mg",    0.57,
  "Cumulative", "12 mg",   1.78
)

or_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(or_sim, or_pub, by = c("endpoint", "regimen"))
or_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("End point" = endpoint, "Regimen vs 6 mg" = regimen,
                "Simulated OR" = OR, "Published OR (Table S1)" = OR_published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Odds ratios of reaching the day-10 end point.")

stopifnot(
  # Centre: the typical simulated OR is within 1.6-fold of Table S1 (log-OR
  # SE is ~0.25 per comparison at n = 200 per arm).
  median(abs(log(or_cmp$OR / or_cmp$OR_published))) < log(1.6),
  # 1.5 mg is far below 6 mg for every end point (published ORs 0.22-0.41,
  # at least 3 SE below 0.8). The 12 mg ORs (1.46-1.8) are too close to 1
  # for a per-row gate at this cohort size.
  all(or_cmp$OR[or_cmp$regimen == "1.5 mg"] < 0.8)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. Its Table 1 apparent clearance implies a
single-dose AUC0-inf of Dose / (CL/F) = 6 mg / 6.27 L/h = 957 ng*h/mL for
the typical 6 mg patient; with log-normal IIV on CL/F, that is also the
expected median of the individual AUC0-inf values. The single 6 mg oral dose of
the PK study is simulated for 200 patients and analysed with PKNCA.

```{r pknca}
ev_sd <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = 1:200, time = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(id = 1:200, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 6, cmt = "depot")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "6 mg single dose") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_sd, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_nca <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  ev_sd |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- tibble::tibble(treatment = "6 mg single dose",
                            aucinf.obs = 6 / 6.27 * 1000)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median AUC0-inf vs Dose / (CL/F) from Table 1. * differs by >20%.")

auc_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::pull(PPORRES) |>
  median(na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(abs(auc_med / (6 / 6.27 * 1000) - 1) < 0.15)
```

The day-10 accumulation of DEX is small (Figure 4), matching the paper's
statement that no substantial accumulation occurs even at 12 mg once daily:

```{r accumulation}
acc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "12 mg", time %in% c(24 + 23, 240 + 23)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_trough = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(acc, digits = 2, caption = "Median DEX trough (ng/mL), 12 mg once daily, after dose 1 and dose 10.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Drug effect driven by the central concentration.** The printed Eqs 4-5
  write the DEX concentration in the inhibition term as `Cp`, the symbol the
  PK equations use for the peripheral compartment. The Supplement 1 Monolix
  code that produced every simulation uses the central concentration `Cc`, and
  Table 2 defines IC50 as a 'DEX plasma concentration'; the model follows the
  code.
- **IIV magnitudes follow the Supplement 1 code.** The Methods say the IIV
  of IC50 and Imax was 'set at 20% of the typical value'; Table 2 and the
  Monolix code give SDs of 0.45 and 0.7 (log scale, IC50) and 0.166 and 0.161
  (logit scale, Imax). The tabulated SDs are used as random-effect SDs on the
  stated log / logit scales, exactly as the Simulx code samples them.
- **Normal lag-time IIV.** tlag is normally distributed in the source
  (Monolix `distribution=normal`), so its random effect is added to tlag in
  hours. The eta keeps the conventional name `etaltlag` but is not applied on
  the log scale; a small fraction of simulated subjects get a negative lag.
- **Fixed PD parameters.** All Table 2 values are encoded with `fixed()`:
  none was estimated in this paper (they were translated from earlier work,
  derived as secondary parameters, or set by assumption or trial-and-error
  simulation).
- **IL-6 drives CRP production without baseline subtraction.** Eq 6 uses the
  absolute IL-6 concentration, `kinCRP * (1 + SIL6onCRP * IL6)`, so the
  registered stimulation factor `sstim_il6_crp` enters with a driver baseline
  of zero.
- **No residual error on TNF-alpha, IL-6 or CRP.** The PD outputs were never
  fitted, so the paper has no residual error model for them; they are model
  states only.
- **Figure 3 regimen.** The paper's Figure 3 caption describes intravenous
  6 mg doses, while the Simulx code doses all regimens into the oral
  absorption compartment. The 6 mg oral regimen is used here; with F unknown,
  an intravenous dose cannot be placed in this apparent-parameter model.
- **Cohort size.** 200 rather than 1000 simulated subjects per regimen.
- **Errata.** PubMed lists no erratum or correction linked to this article
  (checked 2026-10-27).
